title: Despise the Free Lunch
coreMove: Pay the true price so hidden obligations do not buy your freedom cheaply
sourcePressure: Chapter 40 centers on the hidden cost attached to what looks free or cheap. The law values paying the true price because gifts, shortcuts, and bargain access can create obligation, lower standards, or dependency that quietly purchases your freedom. Its limit is that suspicion fails when it becomes paranoid ingratitude or refusal of genuinely fair exchange. Frozen sidecar provides no traceable named anecdote for this chapter; do not fabricate named source anchors.
